original_question: Can the mating construction for two monic polynomials of the same degree be realized by quasiconformal surgery?
target_in_paper: §2, Question 2 of "Quasiconformal Surgery" (Douady, Bielefeld, Shishikura): "Can matings be constructed with quasiconformal surgery?" for the mating of two monic polynomials of the same degree.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact problem the paper asks in §2: it names the mating construction, specifies two monic polynomials of the same degree, and asks whether the construction can be carried out by quasiconformal surgery.
missing_details: The paper is working with complex dynamical systems, i.e. monic polynomials P1,P2 in C[z], not polynomials over an unspecified field.

The relevant notion of mating is the specific topological mating described just before Question 2: compactify each dynamical plane to a closed disk by adjoining the circle at infinity, extend the boundary dynamics by theta -> d theta, glue the circles at infinity, and collapse each external ray to a point.
The intended outcome is not just an informal gluing but a branched self-map of the Riemann sphere that should be conjugate to a rational map of degree d.
The quasiconformal-surgery aspect is tied to the paper's nearby explanation that one seeks a conformal/complex structure preserved by the branched map so that Ahlfors-Bers yields the rational map.

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be distinguished from the separate immediately preceding Question 1, which asks which matings correspond to rational functions at all; your draft does not make that neighboring scope boundary explicit.
The draft does not explicitly state the ambient sphere/dynamical-plane setting in which the mating is performed.
refined_question: Given two complex monic polynomials P1,P2 in C[z] of the same degree d, form their topological mating as in §2 by viewing each polynomial as a map of a closed disk obtained by adjoining the circle at infinity, extending the boundary dynamics by theta -> d theta, gluing the two circles at infinity, and collapsing each external ray to a point; the resulting branched self-map of the sphere is expected to be conjugate to a rational map of degree d. Can this mating be realized by quasiconformal surgery, i.e. by finding a conformal structure preserved by the branched map so that the Ahlfors-Bers theorem produces the corresponding rational map?
justification: The draft clearly targets §2 rather than any other part of the paper. In that section, the paper first explains quasiconformal surgery as producing a branched self-map of the sphere together with a preserved conformal structure, then introduces mating specifically for two monic polynomials of the same degree, and immediately asks as Question 2 whether matings can be constructed with quasiconformal surgery. The rewrite therefore stays narrowly with that exact open problem and only makes explicit the nearby hidden assumptions needed for a stand-alone formulation: the ambient field C, the topological mating procedure being used, the sphere/branched-map viewpoint, and the intended rational-map realization of the same degree d.
